---
title: Under the Hood
type: experiment
order: 80
---

Three stages, chained by `quarto render`, each owned by a different
runtime. None of them ever rewrite your page source:

1. **Pre-render (Python, once per build).** Scans every page in the
   project (even a single-page render triggers a full scan, since that
   page still needs to resolve links against every other page), using
   `quarto inspect` to find "every page" the same way Quarto itself would
   (see `docs/adr/0004-delegate-file-discovery-to-quarto-inspect.md` in
   this repo for why). Falls back to a plain recursive `.qmd`/`.md` walk for a bare
   folder of notes with no `_quarto.yml`, which is what [[CLI|`quarto-graph
   check`]] needs to keep working outside a Quarto project. quarto-graph's
   own `quarto-graph: exclude:` list (see [[Wikilinks and Aliases]]) is
   applied on top of whatever Quarto itself renders. Builds a registry
   (name → page) and a backlink map (page → pages linking to it), merges
   each page's `quarto-graph: sidebar:` override with the project default
   (see [[The Graph Widget]]), and writes it all to a JSON side-channel
   file.
2. **Render (Pandoc, once per page).** A Lua filter reads that registry
   and, for this one page: rewrites wikilinks into real links (see
   [[Wikilinks and Aliases]]), appends the "## Backlinks" section (see
   [[Backlinks]]), stamps a sidebar meta tag if this page's config differs
   from the default, and records this page's real output URL to another
   side-channel file. See `docs/adr/0001-non-destructive-render-time-resolution.md`
   in this repo for why a wikilink resolves to a real URL this late, not up front.
3. **Post-render (Python, once per build).** Joins the pre-render registry
   with every page's real output URL and writes `graph.json` into the
   output directory (see [[The Graph Widget]]).

## Two ways an extension reaches into a project, and they're not the same

`_extensions/quarto-graph/_extension.yml` contributes two different
things, and only one applies automatically:

| Contribution | Applies to your `_quarto.yml` | You still have to write |
|---|---|---|
| `contributes.project` | automatically, the moment `project: type: quarto-graph` names the extension | nothing |
| `contributes.filters` | **not automatically** | `filters: [quarto-graph]`, explicitly |

Confirmed by testing, not just by reading the Quarto docs. A debug print
inside the filter stayed silent on every render until `filters:
[quarto-graph]` was added to the consuming `_quarto.yml`.

## The Python/Lua duplication seam

Python (pre-render) and Lua (the per-page filter) each parse wikilink
syntax independently, because a Lua filter can only see the one page it's
rendering, not the whole project. Both copies of the grammar are kept in
sync by hand — unavoidable inside a two-runtime architecture, not an
oversight. Plain Markdown links don't share this seam: only Python parses
them (see [[Wikilinks and Aliases]]), and by the time Lua sees them
they're already real Pandoc links with nothing left to rewrite.

## Two ways the mini-panel decides not to show up

The `quarto-graph: sidebar:` check doesn't look for `page-layout: full`,
`toc: false`, book-vs-website, or non-HTML formats like `revealjs`/`pdf`/
`dashboard` — none of that is special-cased, on purpose.

`graph.js`'s `mountLocalPanel` looks for the right-margin container
(`#quarto-margin-sidebar`, or the mkdocs-material equivalent) at runtime
with `document.querySelector`, and does nothing if it isn't there. That
single check already covers every layout Quarto can produce, present or
future, because it asks "does this container physically exist," not
"which layout keyword produced this page."

The `quarto-graph: sidebar:` config is a separate, independent check: the
container might exist, but the user might not want the panel there. One
check asks "is there room for this," the other asks "do you want it
here."

## Strict mode

The pre-render script accepts `--strict`, turning any unresolved wikilink
into a build failure instead of a warning — unlike [[CLI|`quarto-graph
check`]], which only ever reports, never fails a build.

The default `pre-render` line in `_extension.yml` (just `prerender.py`) is
auto-resolved by Quarto to wherever the extension got installed, so it
can't carry extra arguments. To enable `--strict`, replace that line with
an explicit command pointing at its real path, e.g. `python3
_extensions/wvictor14/quarto-graph/prerender.py --strict` if you installed
via `quarto add wvictor14/quarto-graph` — check your `_extensions/` folder
for the exact path if you installed it differently.
